nexusClaim.associationBasis: In a prospective case-control study of 40 ENS patients and 40 age- and sex-matched controls, ENS patients had significantly elevated Beck Depression Inventory-II and Beck Anxiety Inventory scores versus controls, improved after nasal reconstruction yet remained significantly worse than controls, and 22.5% carried residual postoperative psychological symptoms with preoperative BDI-II > 28.5 predicting residual burden (Huang 2023); suicidal thoughts were identified in 23 of 62 ENS patients preoperatively and tracked with SNOT-25, ENS6Q, BDI-II, and BAI severity (Huang 2022); the 2025 systematic review pooled 957 ENS patients across 35 articles and concluded the evidence base remains sparse (Hussain 2025).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the case-control design cannot exclude reverse direction (chronic breathlessness dissatisfaction and disability amplify both depression and symptom reporting), the cohort is a single tertiary referral center with surgically selected patients, and the systematic review's evidence-paucity conclusion caps the inference; depression comorbidity in a chronic-symptom population is shared-driver confounded and case-specific review is required.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized chronic-airflow-symptom-burden pathway: persistent paradoxical nasal obstruction despite a patent airway produces disabling breathlessness dissatisfaction, sleep fragmentation, impaired nasal-airway quality of life, and frustration with prior sinus surgery, and this cumulative symptom burden is hypothesized to drive or amplify depressive symptomatology; the reconstruction-linked improvement in BDI-II scores alongside persistent residual symptoms supports a symptom-burden-linked component while showing the mood burden is not fully reversible by airway surgery alone.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The mood association rests on a 40-patient single-center case-control and a suicidal-ideation case series with the systematic review recording evidence paucity; reverse direction and shared tertiary-referral selection cannot be excluded, depression must meet structured diagnostic criteria rather than scale elevations alone, and no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented empty nose syndrome after turbinate-reducing sinonasal surgery with ENS6Q or equivalent instrumentation; structured depression diagnosis (DSM-5 criteria or structured interview) rather than scale elevation alone; chronology of mood symptoms relative to the nasal surgery and ENS onset; exclusion of premorbid mood disorder and independent psychosocial drivers; otolaryngology and psychiatry review of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Premorbid or independent major depressive disorder predating the nasal surgery
Chronic rhinosinusitis recurrence or other active sinonasal disease driving symptoms
Depressive symptoms attributable to opioid, corticosteroid, or other medication exposure

evidenceGaps: Documented empty nose syndrome after turbinate-reducing sinonasal surgery with ENS6Q or equivalent instrumentation; structured depression diagnosis (DSM-5 criteria or structured interview) rather than scale elevation alone; chronology of mood symptoms relative to the nasal surgery and ENS onset; exclusion of premorbid mood disorder and independent psychosocial drivers; otolaryngology and psychiatry review of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the ENS-depression association is prospectively documented against matched controls with dose-response-like severity tracking, but the evidence base is case-series class at a single center, the systematic review records evidence paucity, and the reverse direction is live; no causation or probability is asserted.
